Subject: Capacity bump request + pricing options

Neha —

Quick note from our side: Atlas is seeing a material uptick in inference volume as we ramp a pilot across three new hospitals. We need an interim capacity bump (approx +35% in committed tokens) and would like to understand options for: 1) pricing on the uplift, 2) whether we can co‑term the bumped units to our February renewal, and 3) any short‑term bridging credits while we finalize internal approvals.

Procurement prefers a single invoice cadence and is sensitive to multi‑invoice amendments. Do you have a concise runbook or a few structured options we can evaluate? Happy to set a quick call if helpful.

Thanks —

Head of ML Platforms, Atlas Health

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the heads up and congrats on the pilot traction. We can support a +35% committed uplift mid‑term; below are three practical options with short pros/cons so procurement can evaluate quickly. I attached a draft quote and a one‑pager on bridging credit mechanics.

Option A — Temporary burst + monthly true‑up (lowest friction)\- Add the additional capacity as a time‑boxed monthly uplift for 3 months. No change to annual commit. Token rate is the current committed rate + 10% uplift surcharge. Good if you want no contract amendments and quick onboarding.

Option B — Mid‑term committed top‑up (best unit economics)\- Add permanent committed units pro‑rated to your renewal date and co‑term at next renewal (Feb 2028). We can offer a one‑time uplift discount of 12% off standard uplift rates if you take a 9‑month commitment on the new units. Requires a quick amendment and PO.

Option C — Bridging credit + staged co‑term (balanced)\- We provide a bridging credit (applied to 2 invoices) to offset the initial surcharge while you complete procurement. Then we convert the uplift to committed units that co‑term at Feb 2028. For this we typically require a signed amendment and a 6‑month minimum.

Operational notes:
- Dedicated vs hosted: small differences in latency SLAs and on‑prem pricing (Ben cc'd with details).
- Billing: we can consolidate to a single invoice, but legal will still need an amendment for committed units.
- Attachments: AtlasHealth_Uplift_Quote_v1.pdf (line‑item pricing), BridgeCredit_OnePager.docx (mechanics), MSA_redline_Atlas_2027.pdf (legal redlines suggested).

If procurement is ok we can schedule a 30‑minute alignment call Monday. What time works?

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement likes Option C (bridging credit + staged co‑term) because it minimizes accounting disruption. A few follow ups before we sign: 1) can you confirm the total net cost over the next 9 months under the proposed path and where the bridging credit is applied, 2) we need an invoice cadence of monthly consolidated billing to match our ERP, and 3) legal asked about an evergreen clause in the amendment (we prefer fixed term to avoid auto‑renew traps).

Please send a redline‑friendly amendment and a short cost projection table. If you can have that by EOD Tuesday our procurement lead will review and aim to execute by Friday.

Regards,
Atlas Procurement Team
